Everything here is derivable from the repository — nothing depends on a conversation being remembered. Read it, run the subject guard, continue at next_admissible_unit.

completed_units.result: YES for both conditions. scripts/qm_subject_freeze.py returns INTACT / TRACKED_DRIFT / UNTRACKED_ADDITION / BOTH / UNREADABLE.
completed_units.evidence: Bitten against the real repository: an untracked core/_qm_freeze_probe.py gave exit 2; an appended newline in main.py gave exit 1; both together gave exit 3; main.py restored byte-identically (git hash-object 204c6a93 before and after); baseline exit 0 each time. Made durable in tests/test_qm_subject_freeze.py against a throwaway git repository, including the case that motivates it — a new module under core/ while `git diff --stat` against the snapshot stays empty.
completed_units.anti_vacuity: The one-operation ratchet was asked directly whether it governs the new file: in scope, one definition counted, six files governed. A guard nobody governs is the failure mode this program cannot afford.

completed_units.result: All eight CARRIED_FORWARD. Two map defects found, one code defect banked.

The widened stem index was probed (it resolves 'loop_memory_read') before its silence was trusted, and the sites for C00/C03 were recovered from their closure commits' test imports.

CODE (banked, not fixed): core/loop_memory_read.py:330 describes the deleted planner cache in the present tense. It was written as the correction of an earlier lying comment and outlived its subject by hours.
completed_units.protection_note: UNPROVEN deliberately. Nothing mechanically prevents a future production change from staling a carried-forward cluster silently; the carry-forward derivation is a script run by hand, not a guard in the suite. Whether that instrument should exist is a question for a later unit, not an assumption now.

completed_units.question: Do the map's `file:line` anchors still point at what they name, and are its writer sets complete?
completed_units.result: NO on both, on the map's own acceptance case. Four drifted anchors and a writer set of three where eleven exist. Both classes now guarded.
completed_units.evidence: tests/test_cns_anchor_integrity.py was written first and run against the map as it stood: four failures, every one a real pre-existing defect, none synthetic. The four anchors were all in core/loop_attempt.py and all off by exactly the 24 lines a990e48 removed when it deleted the planner cache — one pointed at a blank line, one at a lone ')', one at 'action_spec={' inside _build_plan, a method that reads nothing of that carrier. The writer finding is stronger than drift: _step_trigger_tls recorded three writers with properties.writers reading PROVEN, and the three are exactly the policy_blocked family, the one path C08 had certified. Checked against history — eleven write sites already existed at b4017bb, the commit that wrote three, and core/loop_step_execution.py has not changed since. The record was wrong when written, not stale.
completed_units.anti_vacuity: The census is asserted to find something before completeness is asserted (>=11 for the thread-local slot, exactly 4 for the list, exactly 0 for the dead field). Rule 1's sub-checks were probed directly: the corrected anchor names its carrier and carries .extend(, the old anchor does not name it at all.
found: MAP: four anchors on failure_history describing sites they no longer occupy.

MAP: _step_trigger_tls understated its producers by 8 of 11. The missing codes are verify_failed, web_empty, timeout, injection_blocked, unknown twice and two variable codes; every one is exercised by tests, so all eight are live sites. injection_blocked is a security-relevant producer that the map's writer set did not contain.
MAP: the existing anchor guard silently skips any anchor whose text carries a suffix, because its digit test fails on 'path:110 (consume)'. Every _step_trigger_tls anchor was therefore unchecked.
completed_units.scope_limitation: Proves that what the map says about writers and anchors matches the code it points at. Does NOT prove the carrier list is complete, nor that a named consumer really consumes.
completed_units.reopens: C08. Its certified arc policy_deny_stops_the_step (M51) rests on the same three writers; the eight unlisted producers of the same carrier were never walked. Per the program's carry-forward rule, a newly discovered producer reopens the unit that generalised from a partial walk.

next_admissible_unit.entry_question: Does the per-type budget in core/replan.py actually decide anything, or does the global cap always fire first in reachable configurations?
next_admissible_unit.why_this_one: C08-U1 could not exercise it: with max_replan_attempts=1 the global cap wins and decision_reason read 'global replan cap reached (1/1)'. A budget that never decides is a different finding from a budget that decides silently, and the codes' max_occurrences (1 for file_not_found, approval_unavailable, injection_blocked and unknown; 2 for the other ten) is the only place the fourteen values differ in CONTROL rather than in text.
next_admissible_unit.planned_probe: Raise max_replan_attempts above the smallest per-type budget and drive the same failure type twice, then read decision_reason. Then bite: change one budget's max_occurrences and predict which pole moves.
next_admissible_unit.watch_for: The trap C08-U1 walked into and named: a domain where the intended mechanism is pre-empted by an unrelated one. State the held configuration before claiming anything about S.
next_admissible_unit.planned_bite_refined: Confirmed read-only before opening the unit: under the DEFAULT cap of 3 the same run reports decision_reason 'injection_blocked budget exhausted (1/1)', so the per-type rule does decide and only the held max_replan_attempts=1 of C08-U1 pre-empted it. The sharper bite is therefore code="injection_blocked" -> code="verify_failed" (budget 2) under the default cap: predict the run no longer aborts on the first occurrence but takes a SECOND attempt — a control difference at L5 rather than a text difference.
